podcast.body: Following "Autobahn," this album saw Kraftwerk abandon all traditional instruments in favor of a purely electronic sound. It also diverged from the progressive rock character of their earlier work, moving towards a new form of pop music, leading it to be considered the first electronic pop album in history. "no es nada descaballado de decir que Radioactivity es el primer disco de pop electrónico de la historia."

podcast.body: Released in the fall of 1975, this album explored the theme of activity on and with the radio. "The next album, Radio Activity from the fall of 1975, was about just that, Activity on and with the radio."

podcast.body: This album was highly admired by David Bowie, who played recordings and video projections of it during his *Station to Station* concerts. Bowie's fascination with *Radio-Activity* was a key indicator of his interest in the Kraurock sound before he embarked on his Berlin period. "David Bowie ponía grabaciones y video proyecciones del radioactividad de Crabbro porque tenía una gran sesión con Crabbro."

podcast.body: This album was out around the time Andy McCluskey saw Kraftwerk play live in 1975, an experience that greatly influenced OMD. "It was the radio activity album, but out of barn had just been a hit."
